scenario.name: AWS CIRT & Unit 42 DFIR — AWS CloudTrail IMDSv1 Role Theft, Off-Instance Replay & S3 Data Events Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a forensic reconstruction of a cloud storage heist from three matching security ledgers: first, catching the tricked web server handing an unguarded temporary building pass out its side window; second, spotting that exact pass suddenly authenticating from a distant street outside the cloud campus; and third, tallying the exact weight of every archive box hauled out of the warehouse to quantify breach scope. In this scenario (T1552.005, AWS CIRT & Unit 42 DFIR, AWS CloudTrail IMDSv1 Role Theft, Off-Instance Replay & S3 Data Events Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: eC2 Instance Metadata Service SSRF Query, then off-Instance STS GetCallerIdentity Replay, then s3 Data Event GetObject Burst. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering EC2 Instance Metadata Service SSRF Query, then Off-Instance STS GetCallerIdentity Replay, then S3 Data Event GetObject Burst, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDSv1) SSRF Query & STS Token Retrieval
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.005 - Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: Abusing a vulnerable web proxy endpoint, the intruder persuades a cloud server to fetch its own local identity drawer over the older unauthenticated channel and hand back its temporary role pass. The attacker sends an HTTP request to a vulnerable web proxy on EC2 instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60001 pointing to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ProdAppInstanceRole. Because IMDSv1 does not require a PUT session token with a TTL hop limit of 1, the metadata endpoint returns the temporary AccessKeyId (ASIA...), SecretAccessKey, and Token (logged in Network Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/, IamRoleName=ProdAppInstanceRole, IssuedAccessKeyPrefix=ASIA... , Temporary STS Credential, ImdsVersion=IMDSv1 , No X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes HTTP SSRF Target: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ProdAppInstanceRole (which Queries the link-local Instance Metadata Service endpoint , http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<RoleName> to retrieve so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "EC2 Instance Metadata Service , IMDSv1 SSRF Query & STS Token Retrieval" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact Returned JSON Fields: AccessKeyId="ASIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", SecretAccessKey, Token, Expiration runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Returned JSON Fields: AccessKeyId="ASIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE", SecretAccessKey, Token, Expiration so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552.005 during "EC2 Instance Metadata Service , IMDSv1 SSRF Query & STS Token Retrieval" , The attacker sends an HTTP request to a vulnerable web proxy on EC2 instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60001 pointing to http://169 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ GET http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ProdAppInstanceRole / ⇠#1 RESP 200) from Node ① (#1 External Host (198.51.100.55)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 S3 Bucket (GetObject Data Log)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Off-Instance STS GetCallerIdentity Replay & GuardDuty OutsideAWS Detection (CloudTrail)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1550.001 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)
stages.description: Moments later, the intruder tests the stolen keycard from an outside internet connection to check who they have become, immediately tripping the cloud campus perimeter sensor that knows an internal server badge should never be swiped from outside. From their external workstation (198.51.100.55, aws-cli/2.15.0 Python/3.11 Linux), the attacker invokes sts:GetCallerIdentity and s3:ListBuckets using the stolen ASIA... EC2 role credentials. stages.title: Stage 3: S3 Data Event GetObject Burst & bytesTransferred Quantification in CloudTrail
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage)
stages.description: With the stolen badge confirmed live, the intruder sweeps through sensitive storage buckets downloading object after object, while investigators tally every single GetObject receipt and byte count to prove exact regulatory impact. The attacker enumerates and downloads sensitive objects from s3://corp-prod-customer-backups/.
